blockers.quote: What If You Knew Your Dream Had a 1 in 2,500 Chance?
blockers.why: K12. Cut at about 40 characters the title reads "What If You Knew Your Dream Had a 1 in 2", a coin flip, while the chip on every thumbnail says 0.04%. The cut title plus the thumbnail no longer says what the video is, and this is the title scored 100.
blockers.fix: What If You Knew the Odds on Your Dream?

suggestions.quote: you take the fat-number placement and stop studying; therefore your mock score falls, and your chip with it, to forty-eight per cent. One sourced comparison, seats against applicants for one exam (to source at G2), shows that a big number is a crowd's base rate, not a verdict on you
suggestions.fix: I would stop watching on this line. I cannot picture a fat-number placement, the mock belongs to the exam I just dropped, and then two facts arrive while I do nothing, on the words base rate, which I would not understand without pausing. Replace it with: You take the office job because its chip reads seventy per cent, and you stop opening the notes. The chip sinks to forty-eight. On the bus home: two thousand five hundred faces, one empty seat. That was the hall's number. His bat is behind the cupboard.

suggestions.quote: it starts from the crowd's base rate and updates from what they do now.
suggestions.fix: It starts as the chance for anyone in this hall, then it moves when you do something.

suggestions.quote: his chip says nought point two
suggestions.fix: Use one unit on every chip: his chip says nought point two per cent; the teacher, three per cent; the chaiwala, sixty-one per cent.

suggestions.quote: The city lit up, built only from people we know: the teacher, the topper at her keyboard, the chaiwala's new board, your cousin's dark chip.
suggestions.fix: I have already seen these four chips, so nothing new happens to me. Cut the tour and put the choice in my hands: The safe seat stays lit. His bat is in your hand. Keep the seat, or give it back.

keep.quote: You find a number tells you what is likely, never what is worth choosing
his chip drains to zero the moment he nods, his hand leaves the bat, and it rolls out of frame
Row three. You don't look up. Out in the lane: thwack.
